subject: Data Engineering
title: Apache Kafka Explained
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Apache Kafka Explained.

hook.text: LinkedIn built Kafka because no existing tool could handle their trillion-message-per-day pipeline.

buildup.text: Kafka is a distributed log. Producers append events to topics. Consumers read at their own pace.

discovery.text: Unlike traditional queues, Kafka retains events for days or weeks. Consumers can replay old messages.

twist.text: Kafka's durability turned it from a message bus into a data platform — the source of truth for events.

climax.text: Today Kafka powers streaming at Netflix, Uber, Airbnb, and most large-scale data platforms.

punchline.text: Kafka doesn't just move data. It remembers it.

quiz.question: What makes Kafka different from traditional message queues?
options: It retains events so consumers can replay old messages
It deletes events immediately after delivery
It only supports one consumer per topic
